description: A grand symmetrical stairwell viewed from an elevated mezzanine or landing position, looking down onto a stair that splits into two flights in a classic bifurcated or horseshoe arrangement. The stair treads are covered in a warm patterned carpet runner in traditional cream and honey tones, and the balustrade features dark-stained wood handrails with slender black metal spindles. The walls are finished in a warm sandy off-white plaster with a slightly rough, organic texture. A high clerestory or transom window above the stairwell landing allows a bright rectangle of natural light to fall from above, illuminating the void. On the landing level at center, a large terracotta or natural stone vessel sits as a statement decorative object, and a full fiddle-leaf fig tree in a planter anchors the right side of the landing, its glossy green leaves spreading upward. Two large abstract artworks in simple frames hang on the right wall, adding graphic interest. Multiple elongated cylindrical column forms in translucent alabaster or marble material hang in a cascading cluster from the ceiling above, at varying heights, their warm amber inner glow filling the stairwell void with warm light and casting illumination downward onto the stair and landing. Camera at elevated height — approximately 7–8 feet — at the top of the upper landing looking steeply down over the bifurcated stair, with a centered symmetrical composition that embraces the architectural symmetry of the paired stair flights below.
